So, if `memory_usage` is in the default prompt order, and the default threshold is `-1`, then new users with a default configuration are going to see the memory usage at all times.

I think this works against the "minimalist, only show information when relevant" design that starship has used up until this point.

Personally, I think if `memory_usage` is going to be in the default prompt, it should have a threshold set. Maybe 75%?
Hmm.. Is the round necessary here, given you have `threshold as f64`?
It's minor, and it might not be worth changing, but you could avoid allocating the string twice here by using `retain` rather than `replace`.

I don't see any specific problem with this, but if we are being consistent with other modules, you would probably set the prefix to empty, and include a separate segment for the icon.

If you did make this change, and name the segment `symbol`, you would get the configuration lookup for free.

+## Memory Usage

+
+By default the swap usage is displayed if the total system swap is non-zero.

+

+| `show_percentage` | `false`               | Display memory usage as a percentage of the available memory. |
+| `show_swap`       | variable              | Display swap usage.                                           |
body: Is `when above zero`, better than `variable` here?

The threshold value the user can set and the threshold we display are in whole units. One thing to know about `format` is that it rounds to whatever place you specify. As a result, for the percentage to display only if it is >= the threshold, we need to round just like `format` does.

Not sure if the user will feel this one, but sure why not 😆

I did some benchmarks, and I noticed that this module was quite slow. Around ~140ms on the MacBook Pro I'm currently on.

It turns out `sysinfo::System::new()` loads all of the system information available (disks, network, processes, etc).

I was able to make the module about 3-4x faster by using this instead:

```
let system = sysinfo::System::new_with_specifics(RefreshKind::new().with_system());
```

This loads just the minimum information required in order to get the memory/swap details.
Good to know, updated with that fix.
